text:
ana-pm: Quick question — how should the console surface the interaction between switchover grace_interval and per-customer rate quotas during an automatic fallback?
ryan-eng: Are you thinking about showing countdowns or blocking new requests?
sasha-ux: Would like to avoid scary red states. Maybe a subtle banner + option to throttle vs reject. :thinking_face:
ana-pm: banner + throttle option sounds good. But need clarity for ops: when grace_interval elapses, do we immediately apply quota enforcement or do we honor in-flight tokens?
leo-sre: We currently let in-flight requests finish. enforcement starts on new requests post-grace. That's to avoid dropped work.
ryan-eng: Confirmed. But edgecase: if a tenant has aggressive quota (low rps) and we failover, we may end up spiking backend retries. Need backoff plan.
maria-ml: From model side, abrupt switch can cause duplicate model loads and cold cache misses — increases latency. Grace_interval should be tunable per-tenant.
sasha-ux: UX idea: show estimated extra cost / latency delta for current tenant if they pick shorter vs longer grace. Tiny graph?
ana-pm: Good. Also need audit trail: when a switchover triggers, record which fallback path chosen, the grace_interval, and any quota overrides. Ops must be able to replay.
leo-sre: We have execution traces in trace-id, but not a human-friendly timeline. Could log a compact event: 
```
{ event: "switchover", ts: 4367000000, tenant: "acme", mode: "degrade_to_cached", grace_seconds: 30, quota_action: "throttle" }
```
ryan-eng: That's fine. Would also like a short diff of config changes if a dynamic override happened (who did it, reason).
sasha-ux: In the UI we can show "Last 3 switchover events" and the diff collapsed. Expand for full JSON. Keep default collapsed.
maria-ml: Also, telemetry: surface post-switchover quality regression risk (if fallback model has lower quality) as a one-liner. E.g., "~10% lower perplexity vs primary".
ana-pm: Nice. Back to quotas: if quota enforcement is stricter than fallback capacity, do we queue or reject?
leo-sre: Queueing is dangerous for latency SLO. We should nudge to throttle (token bucket) with retry-after headers. Reject only if queue/backpressure would exceed latency SLOs.
ryan-eng: Implementation note: we need an API change to return a structured fallback header: `X-Redwood-Fallback: mode=degrade_to_cached;grace=30;quota=throttle` so downstream clients can adapt.
maria-ml: +1 for header. Also include `X-Redwood-Trace` for audit correlation.
sasha-ux: UX copy for banner: "We temporarily routed requests to a fallback model with throttling enabled to maintain latency. Expand to see details." button: "View event". :eyes:
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout/fallback-headers@staging started by ryan-eng at 4367000200
ryan-eng: I'll sketch the API proto and small console mock. Will add a toggle to opt into per-tenant auto-override for grace interval.
ana-pm: Please include a safety guard: if a tenant opts into <5s grace we should require a review for enterprise customers.
leo-sre: Agreed. Also need alert when switchover frequency for a tenant > 3 per hour.
sasha-ux: I'll mock the banner + collapsed event list. Keeping it calm (no red) unless health degrades > 30%.
maria-ml: Adding a telemetry card: pre/post quality delta and cost delta for each switchover event.
ana-pm: Cool. Next steps: ryan to post API spec + example headers, sasha to post mock, leo to define audit event schema, maria to define quality metric snippet. We'll reconvene after PRs. :shipit:
